copy.en: A typhoon and a hurricane are the same kind of storm! They just get different names based on location — typhoon in the western Pacific near the Philippines, hurricane in the Atlantic.
copy.tl: Ang typhoon at hurricane ay parehong uri ng bagyo! Magkaiba lang ang tawag base sa lokasyon — typhoon sa kanlurang Pacific malapit sa Pilipinas, hurricane naman sa Atlantic.
copy.bis: Ang typhoon ug hurricane parehas ra nga matang sa bagyo! Lahi lang ang tawag base sa lokasyon — typhoon sa kasadpang Pacific duol sa Pilipinas, hurricane sa Atlantic.

copy.en:
What exactly is a typhoon?

A typhoon is a huge spinning storm with super strong winds and heavy rain that forms over warm ocean waters!
copy.tl:
Ano ba ang isang bagyo?

Ang bagyo ay isang malaking umiikot na unos na may napakalakas na hangin at malakas na ulan na nabubuo sa mainit na karagatan!
copy.bis:
Unsa man gyud ang bagyo?

Ang bagyo usa ka dakong nagtuyok nga unos nga adunay kusog kaayong hangin ug kusog nga ulan nga matawo sa init nga kadagatan!

copy.en: Typhoons like Typhoon Ulysses can destroy homes, flood large areas, and damage the habitats of many organisms in places like Cagayan Valley and Central Luzon.
copy.tl: Ang mga bagyo tulad ng Typhoon Ulysses ay maaaring sumira ng mga tahanan, bumaha sa malalawak na lugar, at makasira sa mga tirahan ng maraming organismo sa mga lugar tulad ng Cagayan Valley at Central Luzon.
copy.bis: Ang mga bagyo sama sa Typhoon Ulysses makaguba sa mga balay, mobaha sa dagkong mga lugar, ug makaguba sa mga puy-anan sa daghang organismo sa mga lugar sama sa Cagayan Valley ug Central Luzon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: More typhoons reach the Philippines during the wet season

assignedReviews.reason: The card states when typhoons are more frequent but does not describe any effects of weather disturbances, which is the focus of G5-E-8.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: More typhoons reach the Philippines during the wet season
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a seasonal pattern of typhoon occurrence but does not describe typical weather conditions before, during, or after a tropical cyclone as required by G5-E-10.

copy.en:
When do more typhoons reach the Philippines?

More typhoons reach the Philippines during the wet season, especially from June to October!
copy.tl:
Kailan mas maraming bagyo ang dumarating sa Pilipinas?

Mas maraming bagyo ang dumarating sa panahon ng tag-ulan, lalo na mula Hunyo hanggang Oktubre!
copy.bis:
Kanus-a mas daghang bagyo ang moabot sa Pilipinas?

Mas daghang bagyo ang moabot panahon sa ting-ulan, ilabi na gikan sa Hunyo hangtod Oktubre!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It is sound with a frequency above 20,000 Hz
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions sound but does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred in everyday situations. It only defines ultrasound by its frequency, which is not the focus of the competency.

copy.en:
What is ultrasound?

It is sound with a frequency above 20,000 Hz, which humans cannot hear!
copy.tl:
Ano ang ultrasound?

Ito ay tunog na may dalas na mas mataas sa 20,000 Hz, na hindi na kayang marinig ng tao!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang ultrasound?

Kini mao ang tingog nga adunay frequency labaw sa 20,000 Hz, nga dili na madungog sa tawo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: silver chloride darkened just beyond the violet end of the spectrum, revealing ultraviolet light
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the relative wavelengths and frequencies of different types of electromagnetic waves, including radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultra-violet, x-rays, and gamma radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions ultraviolet light as part of the spectrum and its historical discovery; it does not compare wavelengths or frequencies of different electromagnetic waves.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In 1801, silver chloride darkened just beyond the violet end of the spectrum
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a discovery event but does not identify a scientist or an invention, so it does not support the competency.

copy.en:
How was ultraviolet light first discovered?

In 1801, silver chloride darkened just beyond the violet end of the spectrum, revealing ultraviolet light!
copy.tl:
Paano natuklasan ang ultraviolet light noong una?

Noong 1801, nag-itim ang silver chloride lampas sa violet na dulo ng spectrum, at doon natuklasan ang ultraviolet light!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkadiskubre sa ultraviolet light sa una?

Niadtong 1801, miitom ang silver chloride unahan sa violet nga tumoy sa spectrum, ug mao kini ang nagpakita sa ultraviolet light!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the edge is blurry because of the penumbra
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses shadow edge blurriness and penumbra, which is a light-behavior topic, but it does not support the Grade 3 competency of participating in guided activities to explore and describe sources of light, how light behaves or can be changed, and its uses. The penumbra concept is advanced and not aligned with the grade-level activity or content.

copy.en: Many think every shadow has a clean, sharp edge. But in truth, the edge is blurry because of the penumbra, where the dark slowly fades into light!
copy.tl: Akala ng marami, malinaw at matalim ang gilid ng bawat anino. Pero ang totoo, malabo ang gilid dahil sa penumbra kung saan unti-unting nawawala ang dilim papunta sa liwanag!
copy.bis: Naghunahuna ang daghan nga ang ngilit sa matag landong tin-aw ug hait. Apan ang tinuod, hanap ang ngilit tungod sa penumbra, diin ang kangitngit hinay-hinay nga mawala paingon sa kahayag!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the dark center where you are is the umbra itself
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the umbra, a shadow concept related to light behavior, but it does not guide students to explore or describe sources of light, how light behaves or can be changed, or its everyday uses as required by G3-F-6. The umbra is an advanced shadow term not aligned with the grade 3 competency's scope.

copy.en: Can you stand inside an umbra? Yes! When you stand in the shadow of a big object at noon, the dark center where you are is the umbra itself!
copy.tl: Pwede bang tumayo sa loob ng umbra? Oo! Kapag nakatayo ka sa anino ng malaking bagay tuwing tanghali, ang madilim na gitna kung nasaan ka ay ang umbra mismo!
copy.bis: Makatindog ba sa sulod sa umbra? Oo! Kon nagtindog ka sa landong sa dako nga butang panghaponon, ang ngitngit nga tunga diin ka naa mao ang umbra mismo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They use the soft penumbra to make shadows gentle instead of sharp!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a use of light (stage lighting) and the term penumbra, but it does not guide students to explore or describe sources of light, how light behaves, or how it can be changed. It is a single factual statement about stage lighting, not an instructional activity or description of light behavior. The competency requires participation in guided science activities to explore and describe light sources, behavior, and uses; this card only touches on a specific use without supporting the exploration or description.

copy.en:
Why do stage shows use soft shadows?

They use the soft penumbra to make shadows gentle instead of sharp! This makes the scene look pleasant and easy on the eyes.
copy.tl:
Bakit gumagamit ng malalambot na anino ang mga stage show?

Ginagamit nila ang malabong penumbra para maging malambot ang anino! Kaya mas maganda ang tanawin at hindi nakakagulat sa mata.
copy.bis:
Nganong naggamit og humok nga landong ang mga stage show?

Gigamit nila ang hanap nga penumbra aron mahimong humok ang landong! Mao nga mas nindot tan-awon ug dili makapakurat sa mata.

assignedReviews.reason: The card defines an unconformity as a gap in the rock record, which is a concept related to geologic time, but it does not describe relative or absolute dating techniques or how they determine subdivisions of geologic time. assignedReviews.card_evidence: An unconformity is a gap in the rock record! Some layers are missing due to erosion or no sediment, making spans of time absent.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the geologic time scale helps to recount the history of the Earth

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some layers are missing due to erosion or no sediment

copy.en: An unconformity is a gap in the rock record! Some layers are missing due to erosion or no sediment, making spans of time absent.
copy.tl: Ang unconformity ay isang puwang sa rock record! Nawawala ang ilang layer dahil sa erosion o walang sediment, kaya may nawawalang yugto ng panahon.
copy.bis: Ang unconformity usa ka gintang sa rock record! Nawala ang pipila ka layer tungod sa erosion o walay sediment, busa adunay nawala nga mga yugto sa panahon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It often flows through hidden underground rivers right inside the caves!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a karst landform and underground rivers, which are types of landforms/bodies of water, but it does not identify local examples or describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment. It only states a general fact about water flow in karst areas, providing no direct instructional support for the competency's required actions.

copy.en:
Where does water flow in karst land?

It often flows through hidden underground rivers right inside the caves!
copy.tl:
Saan dumadaloy ang tubig sa lupaing karst?

Madalas itong dumadaloy sa mga ilog sa ilalim ng lupa sa loob ng mga kuweba!
copy.bis:
Asa modagayday ang tubig sa yutang karst?

Kasagaran kining modagayday sa mga suba sa ilawom sa yuta sulod sa mga langob!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A fair test needs the same type of person or thing
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches the concept of a fair test and controlling variables, using a boy and girl eating rice as an example. It has no content about how sound is made or transferred, which is the subject of G3-F-4.

copy.en:
Why is it unfair to compare a boy who ate rice with a girl who ate rice?

Because being a boy or a girl is another variable that changed! A fair test needs the same type of person or thing, so you can see only the effect of the rice.
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi patas na ikumpara ang isang batang lalaki na kumain ng kanin sa isang batang babae na kumain ng kanin?

Dahil ang pagiging lalaki o babae ay isa pang variable na nagbago! Kailangan ng fair test ng parehong uri ng tao o bagay, para makita mo lang ang epekto ng kanin.
copy.bis:
Nganong dili patas nga ikumpara ang usa ka batang lalaki nga mikaon ug kan-on sa usa ka batang babaye nga mikaon ug kan-on?

Tungod kay ang pagkahimong lalaki o babaye usa pa ka variable nga nausab! Ang fair test nagkinahanglan ug parehong klase sa tawo o butang, aron makita nimo ang epekto lamang sa kan-on.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It was named after the inventor James Watt.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card names James Watt as an inventor but does not identify any specific invention of his. The competency requires identifying a scientist and their invention/s; the card only mentions the scientist and the unit named after him, not the invention itself.

copy.en:
Who is the watt named after?

The watt (W) is the unit of power! It was named after the inventor James Watt.
copy.tl:
Kanino ipinangalan ang watt?

Ang watt (W) ang yunit ng power o lakas! Ipinangalan ito kay imbentor na si James Watt.
copy.bis:
Kang kinsa ginganlan ang watt?

Ang watt (W) ang yunit sa power o gahum! Ginganlan kini sa imbentor nga si James Watt.

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses units of size and measuring tools (ruler, meter stick). It does not mention any science invention, nor does it ask students to identify an invention from home/community or explain its impact on everyday life. The content is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Size is measured in inches or meters, and a ruler or meter stick is used to find the exact measurement.
copy.tl: Ang sukat ay sinusukat sa inches o metro, at ang ruler o meter stick ay ginagamit upang malaman ang eksaktong sukat.
copy.bis: Ang gidak-on gisukod sa inches o metro, ug ang ruler o meter stick gigamit aron mahibaloan ang eksaktong sukod.

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses units of time for describing motion duration. It does not address particle arrangement, spacing, or motion in states of matter, which is the focus of G7-M-4.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Time is expressed in seconds, minutes, or hours
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Time is expressed in seconds, minutes, or hours
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe properties of solids, liquids, or gases in terms of shape and volume. It is unrelated to states of matter.

copy.en: Time is expressed in seconds, minutes, or hours, and these units help us describe how long a motion lasts.
copy.tl: Ang time ay ipinapahayag sa seconds, minutes, o hours, at ang mga yunit na ito ay tumutulong sa atin na ilarawan kung gaano katagal ang isang motion.
copy.bis: Ang time gipahayag sa seconds, minutes, o hours, ug kini nga mga yunit makatabang kanato sa paghulagway kung unsa kadugay ang usa ka motion.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Universal indicator turns GREEN at neutral!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify common acids, bases, and salts (e.g., hydrochloric acid, sodium hydroxide, and saline solution) using different indicators
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the color of universal indicator at pH 7. copy.en: Universal indicator turns GREEN at neutral! When the pH is exactly 7, the liquid becomes green.
copy.tl: Ang universal indicator ay nagiging BERDE sa neutral! Kapag ang pH ay 7, ang likido ay nagiging berde.
copy.bis: Ang universal indicator mahimong BERDE sa neutral! Kung ang pH kay 7, ang likido mahimong berde.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It shows the whole pH scale from 0 (acid) to 14 (base)!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify common acids, bases, and salts (e.g., hydrochloric acid, sodium hydroxide, and saline solution) using different indicators
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes what a universal indicator displays (the pH scale), but it does not identify any common acids, bases, or salts, nor does it show how to use indicators to identify such substances. It only provides background about an indicator's range.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It shows the whole pH scale from 0 (acid) to 14 (base)!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify solutions, which can be found at home and in school and that react with litmus indicator, as acids, bases, and salts
assignedReviews.reason: The competency focuses on identifying home/school solutions as acids, bases, or salts using litmus indicator. The card mentions a universal indicator and pH range but does not involve litmus, specific solutions, or identification of acids/bases/salts.

copy.en:
What does a universal indicator show?

It shows the whole pH scale from 0 (acid) to 14 (base)!
copy.tl:
Ano ang ipinapakita ng universal indicator?

Ipinapakita nito ang buong pH scale mula 0 (asido) hanggang 14 (base)!
copy.bis:
Unsay gipakita sa universal indicator?

Nagpakita kini sa tibuok pH scale gikan 0 (asido) ngadto 14 (base)!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The universe is filled with countless galaxies
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how modern research about celestial objects uses new space technologies including telescopes and space probes
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that there are billions of galaxies with billions of stars. It does not mention telescopes, space probes, or modern research methods, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The universe is filled with countless galaxies
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses galaxies and stars, which are celestial objects, but it does not involve guided observation or description of the Sun, Moon, planets, and stars commonly seen in the sky. It is only broadly related to celestial objects.

copy.en:
How many galaxies are out there?

Billions and billions! The universe is filled with countless galaxies, and every single one holds billions of stars.
copy.tl:
Ilang galaxy ang nasa sansinukob?

Bilyon-bilyon! Puno ang sansinukob ng maraming galaxy, at bawat isa ay may bilyon-bilyong bituin.
copy.bis:
Pila ka galaxy ang naa sa uniberso?

Bilyon-bilyon! Puno ang uniberso og daghan kaayong galaxy, ug ang matag usa adunay bilyon-bilyon ka bituon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Uranus has 27 known moons!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a specific fact about Uranus's moons and their naming, but does not describe the general structure of the solar system, nor identify major celestial objects' main features or composition. It is only tangentially related to the solar system topic.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Uranus has 27 known moons!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a planet and its moons, which are celestial objects, but it does not support guided observation or description of natural objects commonly seen in the sky. It is a factual trivia about moon names, not an activity or description of observable sky objects.

copy.en: Uranus has 27 known moons! All of them are named after characters from William Shakespeare and poet Alexander Pope, like Miranda, Ariel, Titania, and Oberon.
copy.tl: Ang Uranus ay may 27 kilalang buwan! Lahat sila ay pinangalanan sa mga karakter ni William Shakespeare at ng poet na si Alexander Pope, tulad nina Miranda, Ariel, Titania, at Oberon.
copy.bis: Ang Uranus adunay 27 ka nahibaloan nga mga buwan! Tanan niini ginganlan sa mga karakter ni William Shakespeare ug sa poet nga si Alexander Pope, sama nila Miranda, Ariel, Titania, ug Oberon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: One day on Uranus lasts about 17 hours!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a single fact about Uranus's rotation period. It does not describe the general structure of the solar system, identify major celestial objects, or address their main features and composition.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: One day on Uranus lasts about 17 hours!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: Uranus is a planet, but the card does not involve observing or describing natural objects seen in the sky; it only states a rotation-period fact.

copy.en:
How long is a day on Uranus?

One day on Uranus lasts about 17 hours! That is the exact time it takes for the planet to complete one day.
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal ang isang araw sa Uranus?

Ang isang araw sa Uranus ay tumatagal ng mga 17 oras! Iyon ang saktong panahon para makumpleto ng planeta ang isang araw.
copy.bis:
Unsa kadugay ang usa ka adlaw sa Uranus?

Ang usa ka adlaw sa Uranus molungtad ug mga 17 ka oras! Mao kini ang eksakto nga panahon aron makompleto sa planeta ang usa ka adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Uranus spins tilted almost on its side
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a planet, which is a celestial object, but it does not involve guided observation or description of objects commonly seen in the sky, and Uranus is not a typical naked-eye object for Grade 3 observation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Uranus spins tilted almost on its side
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a specific fact about Uranus's axial tilt but does not describe the general structure of the solar system, major celestial objects, their main features, or composition. It is a single planetary detail, not direct support for the competency.

copy.en:
Which planet rolls along its orbit like a ball?

Uranus spins tilted almost on its side, making it the only planet that seems to roll along its orbit!
copy.tl:
Aling planeta ang gumugulong sa orbit nito parang bola?

Ang Uranus ay umiikot nang nakatagilid, halos nakahiga, kaya ito ang tanging planeta na parang gumugulong sa orbit nito!
copy.bis:
Hining planeta ang nagligid sa orbit niini murag bola?

Ang Uranus molibot nga nakahapay, halos nakahigda, mao nga kini ra ang planeta nga morag nagligid sa orbit niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Concrete and asphalt absorb solar heat

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions heat absorption by materials but does not identify examples of conduction, convection, or radiation, nor their advantages/disadvantages. It only touches on heat in a general urban context.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Concrete and asphalt absorb solar heat
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions heat energy causing a temperature change, but does not explicitly identify energy as something that can cause change across light, sound, and heat. It only describes a specific heat-related effect without teaching the broader concept.

copy.en: The urban heat island effect makes cities like Manila several degrees hotter! Concrete and asphalt absorb solar heat, while trees and vegetation are reduced.
copy.tl: Ang urban heat island effect ay nagpapainit sa mga lungsod tulad ng Maynila ng ilang degree! Sumasipsip ng init ang kongkreto at aspalto, habang nababawasan ang mga puno.
copy.bis: Ang urban heat island effect nagapainit sa mga lungsod sama sa Maynila sa pipila ka degree! Nagsipsip og init ang kongkreto ug aspalto samtang ang mga puno ug tanom nabawasan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Usain Bolt's 100-meter world record is 9.58 seconds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a distance (100 m) and a time (9.58 s) but never states that speed is distance divided by time or defines speed. It is a factual record, not instruction on the concept of speed.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Usain Bolt's 100-meter world record is 9.58 seconds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure accurately the distance and time when things move using simple equipment

copy.en:

Ano ang 100-meter world record ni Usain Bolt?

Ang 100-meter world record ni Usain Bolt ay 9.58 seconds, na itinakda noong 2009!

Unsa ang 100-meter world record ni Usain Bolt?

Ang 100-meter world record ni Usain Bolt mao ang 9.58 seconds, gibutang niadtong 2009!

copy.tl: Ang electromagnetic waves ay ginagamit sa telecommunication, pagluluto, at medical sciences - dala nila ang tawag sa iyong telepono, pinapainit ang pagkain sa microwave, at tinutulungan ang mga doktor na makita ang loob ng katawan.

How does the uterus nourish a developing baby?

It holds the fertilized egg and provides a rich lining that feeds the growing embryo until it becomes a fully developed baby.
copy.tl:
Paano pinapakain ng uterus ang lumalaking sanggol?

Hawak nito ang fertilized egg at nagbibigay ng masaganang lining na nagpapakain sa lumalaking embryo hanggang maging ganap na sanggol.
copy.bis:
Unsaon sa uterus pag-amuma sa nagtubo nga bata?

Kini nagkupot sa fertilized egg ug naghatag ug daghan nga lining nga nagpakaon sa nagtubo nga embryo hangtod mahimo nga hingpit nga bata.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the relative wavelengths and frequencies of different types of electromagnetic waves, including radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultra-violet, x-rays, and gamma radiation

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe electromagnetic radiation (EMR) as energy that is created by the vibrations of electrically charged particles which allows it to travel through materials or space as transverse waves

copy.en:
Why do some things glow under ultraviolet light?

They glow because the ultraviolet light hits them and magically turns into visible light!
copy.tl:
Bakit kumikinang ang ilang bagay kapag tinamaan ng ultraviolet?

Kumikinang sila dahil tinatamaan sila ng ultraviolet at nagiging nakikitang liwanag!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga naggilak ang ubang butang kon maigo sa ultraviolet?

Naggilak sila tungod kay maigo sila sa ultraviolet ug mahimong makitang kahayag!

copy.en: After the germ used in a vaccine is grown, it gets purified, measured into correct doses, and filled into clean vials before being shipped to clinics.
copy.tl: Pagkatapos patubuin ang mikrobyo na gagamitin sa bakuna, nililinis ito, sinusukat sa tamang dosis, at inilalagay sa malilinis na bote bago ipadala sa mga klinika.
copy.bis: Human matubo ang mikrobyo nga gamiton sa bakuna, limpyohan kini, sukdon sa saktong dosis, ug ibutang sa limpyo nga botelya sa dili pa ipadala sa mga klinika.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it has no air pressure
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air pressure but only in the context of a vacuum (no air), not as a characteristic used to describe weather. It does not teach weather characteristics such as air temperature, wind, humidity, etc.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A vacuum is a space with no air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a vacuum as a space with no air, which touches on the idea of space but does not describe matter as having mass and taking up space. It does not directly support the competency's definition of matter.

copy.en: A vacuum is a space with no air, so it has no air pressure — just like in outer space!
copy.tl: Ang vacuum ay isang lugar na walang hangin, kaya wala rin itong air pressure — gaya ng nasa kalawakan!
copy.bis: Ang vacuum usa ka dapit nga walay hangin, busa wala usab kini air pressure — sama sa kawanangan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That's why drinking water every day is so important.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that drinking water is important, which touches on water as a need, but it does not identify water as one of the basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter). The main content is about the percentage of water in the body, not about basic needs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That's why drinking water every day is so important.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that water is one of the basic needs of plants and animals
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the importance of drinking water for humans, but it does not recognize water as a basic need of plants and animals. It focuses on the human body's water content, not on water as a need for living things generally.

copy.en:
How much of your body is water?

About 60% of an adult's body is water — that's more than half! That's why drinking water every day is so important.
copy.tl:
Gaano karami ang tubig sa katawan mo?

Mga 60% ng katawan ng isang matanda ay tubig — mahigit kalahati! Kaya napakahalaga ng pag-inom ng tubig araw-araw.
copy.bis:
Pila ka porsyento sa lawas nimo ang tubig?

Mga 60% sa lawas sa hamtong nga tawo kay tubig — kapin sa katunga! Mao nga importante kaayo ang pag-inom og tubig matag adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: grown-ups have 32 permanent teeth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the number of adult teeth; it does not describe how any human body system works, including the skeletal or digestive system.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Kids have 20 milk teeth, but grown-ups have 32 permanent teeth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a change from childhood to adulthood but does not teach the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Kids have 20 milk teeth, but grown-ups have 32 permanent teeth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a tooth count for children and adults but does not compare life cycles of mammals, birds, or plants.

copy.en:
How many teeth do adults have?

Kids have 20 milk teeth, but grown-ups have 32 permanent teeth — including the wisdom teeth!
copy.tl:
Ilang ngipin ang mayroon ang matatanda?

Ang mga bata ay may 20 gatas na ngipin, pero ang matatanda ay may 32 permanenteng ngipin — kasama na ang wisdom teeth!
copy.bis:
Pila ka ngipon ang naa sa mga hamtong?

Ang mga bata adunay 20 ka gatas nga ngipon, apan ang mga hamtong adunay 32 ka permanente nga ngipon — lakip na ang wisdom teeth!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: one giant single cell
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card presents a trivia fact that an ostrich egg yolk is a single cell, but it does not teach the distinction between unicellular and multicellular organisms, nor does it provide examples like bacteria or humans. It only mentions a single cell without addressing organism-level organization.

copy.en:
What is the largest single cell on Earth?

It's the yolk of an ostrich egg! That yellow part is one giant single cell — the biggest among all living things.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamalaking iisang cell?

Ang yolk (dilaw) ng itlog ng ostrich! Ang dilaw na bahaging iyon ay isang napakalaking cell — ang pinakamalaki sa lahat ng buhay na bagay.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakadako nga usa ka cell?

Ang yolk sa itlog sa ostrich! Kanang dalag nga bahin usa ka dako kaayo nga cell — ang pinakadako sa tanang buhi nga butang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's about 384,000 kilometers away!

The card provides a factual distance but does not support observing, describing, or participating in guided activities about the Moon's appearance or behavior. It is only related vocabulary.

copy.en:
How far is the Moon from Earth?

It's about 384,000 kilometers away! That makes the Moon the closest object in space to us.
copy.tl:
Gaano kalayo ang Buwan mula sa Earth?

Nasa mga 384,000 kilometro ito! Kaya ang Buwan ang pinakamalapit na bagay sa kalawakan sa atin.
copy.bis:
Unsa kalayo ang Bulan gikan sa Earth?

Mga 384,000 ka kilometro kini! Mao nga ang Bulan ang labing duol nga butang sa kawanangan kanato.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Acceleration is the change in speed over time—speeding up or slowing down!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces cause objects to accelerate, and that acceleration of an object is its rate of change of velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines acceleration as change in speed over time, but does not mention forces causing acceleration or the rate of change of velocity. It only touches on a simplified notion of acceleration, not the competency's core content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Acceleration is the change in speed over time—speeding up or slowing down!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate in practical situations and describe that acceleration is a change in speed and/or direction as the result of a net force
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes acceleration as change in speed, but does not address the role of net force or change in direction. It lacks the practical demonstration and net-force connection required by the competency.

copy.en:
What is acceleration?

Acceleration is the change in speed over time—speeding up or slowing down! Press the gas pedal? That's positive acceleration. Hit the brakes? That's acceleration too—just decreasing speed.
copy.tl:
Ano ang acceleration?

Ang acceleration ay pagbabago ng bilis sa paglipas ng oras—bumibilis o bumagal! Tinapakan ang gas? Positibong acceleration. Nagpreno? Acceleration din—bumabagal lang.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang acceleration?

Ang acceleration mao ang pagbag-o sa katulin—mopaspas o mohinay! Tunob sa gas? Positibo nga acceleration. Mopreno? Accelereration usab—mohinay lang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It sprints almost 100 kilometers per hour to chase prey!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a speed value (100 km/h) but does not teach the concept that speed is how far an object moves in a given time. It provides an example of speed without defining or explaining the relationship between distance and time.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It sprints almost 100 kilometers per hour to chase prey!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: construct and label simple graphs of different speeds including stationary and uniform speeds, both fast and slow
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses speed but does not involve constructing or labeling any graphs of speeds, stationary or uniform. It offers no graphical representation or comparison of different speeds.

copy.en:
Did you know the cheetah is the fastest land animal?

It sprints almost 100 kilometers per hour to chase prey! But it gets tired fast, so it can only keep this speed for a few seconds.
copy.tl:
Alam mo ba na ang cheetah ang pinakamabilis na hayop sa lupa?

Tumatakbo ito nang halos 100 kilometers per hour para habulin ang biktima! Pero mabilis itong mapagod, kaya ilang segundo lang kayang panatilihin ang bilis na ito.
copy.bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga ang cheetah mao ang pinakapaspas nga hayop sa yuta?

Modagan kini og hapit 100 kilometers per hour aron gukdon ang biktima! Apan paspas kini kapuyon, mao nga pipila lang ka segundo mahuptan kini nga katulin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Constant speed means an object never speeds up or slows down.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: construct and label simple graphs of different speeds including stationary and uniform speeds, both fast and slow
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines constant speed but does not involve constructing or labeling any graph of speeds, which is the core action of G4-F-4. It only mentions uniform speed conceptually, without any graphical representation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it covers equal distances in equal amounts of time
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies the distance-time relationship of speed but does not explicitly identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed. It provides background understanding of uniform motion rather than directly teaching the definition of speed.

copy.en: Constant speed means an object never speeds up or slows down. Like a cruising plane, it covers equal distances in equal amounts of time, staying perfectly steady!
copy.tl: Ang constant speed ay nangangahulugang hindi bumibilis o bumabagal ang isang bagay. Tulad ng lumilipad na eroplano, tinatahak nito ang pantay na layo sa parehong oras, nananatiling steady!
copy.bis: Ang constant speed nagpasabot nga ang butang dili mopaspas o mohinay. Sama sa naglubad nga eroplano, molupad kini sa parehas nga gilay-on sa parehas nga oras, magpabilin nga steady!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Multiply speed by time for distance. Divide distance by speed for time.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card uses speed as a given quantity and shows how to compute distance or time, but it never states the definition that speed is how far an object moves in a given time. It does not directly teach the concept required by G4-F-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Multiply speed by time for distance. Divide distance by speed for time.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure accurately the distance and time when things move using simple equipment
assignedReviews.reason: The card involves distance and time calculations but does not describe measuring distance and time using simple equipment. It is a formula-based calculation card, not a measurement activity, so it does not directly support G4-F-2.

copy.en:
How can you find a missing speed, distance, or time?

Know two, find the third! Multiply speed by time for distance. Divide distance by speed for time. At 60 km/h, a 120-kilometer trip takes exactly 2 hours!
copy.tl:
Paano mo mahahanap ang nawawalang bilis, layo, o oras?

Alamin ang dalawa, hanapin ang pangatlo! I-multiply ang bilis at oras para sa layo. Hatiin ang layo sa bilis para sa oras. Sa 60 km/h, 2 oras ang 120 kilometers!
copy.bis:
Unsaon nimo pagpangita sa nawala nga katulin, gilay-on, o oras?

Nahibal-an ang duha, pangitaa ang ikatulo! I-multiply ang katulin ug oras para sa gilay-on. Bahinon ang gilay-on sa katulin para sa oras. Sa 60 km/h, 2 ka oras ang 120 kilometers!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rolling balls slow down and stop because of friction
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan and carry out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on the size of frictional forces
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that friction slows a ball, but the competency requires planning and carrying out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on frictional forces. The card provides no investigation, no comparison of surfaces, and no measurement of frictional force.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Friction fights motion to reduce speed
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to demonstrate that pushes and pulls can be used to change the speed and direction of an object including making it go faster, turn it to a different direction, slow it down, and stop it
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about using pushes and pulls to change speed and direction. The card describes friction as a force that slows motion, but does not address pushes or pulls, nor does it demonstrate how applied forces change speed or direction. It only mentions slowing, not the push/pull mechanism.

copy.en: Rolling balls slow down and stop because of friction, the rubbing between the ball and floor. Friction fights motion to reduce speed. Without it, the ball would roll forever!
copy.tl: Bumabagal at tumitigil ang bola dahil sa friction, ang pagkuskos ng bola at sahig. Lumalaban ang friction sa galaw para pabagalin ang bilis. Kung wala ito, magpapatuloy ang bola nang walang tigil!
copy.bis: Mohinay ug mohunong ang bola tungod sa friction, ang pagkuskos sa bola ug salog. Supak ang friction sa lihok aron pakunhuron ang katulin. Kung walay friction, magpadayon ang bola sa pagligid nga walay hunong!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Light zooms at about 300,000 kilometers per second
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the speed of light. It does not address sources of light, how light behaves or can be changed, or its uses in everyday situations, which are the focus of G3-F-6.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Light zooms at about 300,000 kilometers per second
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions light but does not connect light to the concept of energy causing change, nor does it include sound or heat. It does not directly support the competency's goal of identifying energy as something that can cause change.

copy.en: Light zooms at about 300,000 kilometers per second (186,000 miles per second)! It is the absolute fastest thing in the entire universe.
copy.tl: Ang liwanag ay tumatagos nang mga 300,000 kilometro kada segundo (186,000 milya kada segundo)! Ito ang pinakamabilis na bagay sa buong sansinukob.
copy.bis: Ang kahayag mobaktas mga 300,000 ka kilometro kada segundo (186,000 ka milya kada segundo)! Kini ang labing paspas nga butang sa tibuok uniberso.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sound travels through air at about 343 meters per second
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a speed value for sound and compares it to light, but does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred in everyday situations. It does not support the skill of describing sound production or transfer.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sound travels through air at about 343 meters per second
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions sound but does not identify energy as something that can cause change, nor does it address light, sound, or heat energy as forms of energy causing change. It only states a speed fact and a lightning/thunder observation.

copy.en: Sound travels through air at about 343 meters per second (1,235 km/h). It is much slower than light, so you see lightning before hearing thunder!
copy.tl: Ang tunog ay naglalakbay sa hangin nang mga 343 metro kada segundo (1,235 km/h). Mas mabagal ito kaysa liwanag, kaya nauuna mong makita ang kidlat bago ang kulog!
copy.bis: Ang tingog mobaktas sa hangin og 343 ka metro kada segundo (1,235 km/h). Mas hinay kaysa kahayag, mao nga makita una ang kilat sa dili pa madungog ang dalugdog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Faster vehicles need longer distances to stop!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions speed and stopping distance but does not define speed as distance per unit time, which is the core of G4-F-3. It only uses the idea of speed in a safety context.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Faster vehicles need longer distances to stop!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces cause objects to accelerate, and that acceleration of an object is its rate of change of velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses reaction time and stopping distance but does not address forces, acceleration, or velocity as rate of change. It does not support the competency's content.

copy.en: Faster vehicles need longer distances to stop! This includes reaction time, the seconds before a driver hits the brakes. That is why slow speeds near schools are so important for safety.
copy.tl: Mas mahaba ang kailangang layo para huminto ng mabilis na sasakyan! Kasama rito ang reaction time, ang oras bago tumugon ang drayber. Kaya mahalaga ang mabagal na bilis malapit sa eskwelahan para sa kaligtasan.
copy.bis: Paspas nga sakyanan nagkinahanglan og mas taas nga gilay-on aron mohunong! Apil niini ang reaction time, ang oras ayha motubag ang drayber. Mao nga importante ang hinay duol sa eskwelahan para safe.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a steeper line means faster movement, while a flat line means standing still
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: construct and label simple graphs of different speeds including stationary and uniform speeds, both fast and slow
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches how to interpret speed from a distance-time graph's line shape, but G4-F-4 requires constructing and labeling simple graphs of different speeds. The card does not support graph construction or labeling.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a steeper line means faster movement, while a flat line means standing still
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe uniform velocity and represent it using distance-time graphs
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a basic interpretation of distance-time graph slopes, but it does not describe uniform velocity explicitly nor show how to represent it using distance-time graphs. It is only related background.

copy.en: On a distance-time graph, a steeper line means faster movement, while a flat line means standing still. You can easily tell the speed just by looking at the line's shape!
copy.tl: Sa distance-time graph, ang mas tarik na linya ay mas mabilis, habang ang patag na linya ay nakatigil. Madali mong masasabi ang bilis sa pamamagitan lang ng pagtingin sa hugis ng linya!
copy.bis: Sa distance-time graph, ang mas tarik nga linya mas paspas, samtang ang patag nga linya naghunong. Masulti nimo ang katulin pinaagi lang sa pagtan-aw sa porma sa linya!

copy.en:
Is there a single "true speed" for everything?

Nope! Speed depends on your reference point. Walking inside a moving bus makes you slow compared to passengers, but super fast compared to someone standing on the road!
copy.tl:
May iisang "tunay na bilis" ba para sa lahat?

Hindi! Nakadepende ang bilis sa iyong sukatan. Paglakad sa tumatakbong bus ay mabagal kumpara sa pasahero, pero napakabilis kumpara sa taong nakatayo sa kalsada!
copy.bis:
Aduna ba'y usa ra ka "tinuod nga katulin" para sa tanan?

Dili! Nagdepende ang katulin sa imong sukdanan. Paglakaw sa nagdagan nga bus hinay kumpara sa pasahero, apan paspas kaayo kumpara sa tawo nga nagtindog sa dalan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Walking is about 5 km/h, but jogging is 10 km/h or more!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions speed values (km/h) but does not define speed as distance per unit time, which is the core of the competency. It only compares speeds without explaining the concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Running is twice as fast, so you arrive quicker
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: construct and label simple graphs of different speeds including stationary and uniform speeds, both fast and slow
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses fast and slow speeds but does not involve constructing or labeling any graphs, which is the required activity for this competency.

copy.en: Walking is about 5 km/h, but jogging is 10 km/h or more! Running is twice as fast, so you arrive quicker, but you also tire out much more easily!
copy.tl: Ang lakad ay mga 5 km/h, pero ang takbo ay 10 km/h o mas mabilis pa! Doble ang bilis ng takbo kaya mas mabilis makarating, pero mas madali ka ring mapagod!
copy.bis: Ang lakaw mga 5 km/h, pero ang dagan 10 km/h o labaw pa! Doble ang katulin sa dagan busa mas paspas makaabot, apan mas dali usab ka mapuy-an!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Sun is a star and the closest one to us!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Sun is a star and the closest one to us!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some of the overall characteristics of the Sun, such as its composition, its size, and the main energy it radiates
assignedReviews.reason: The competency asks to describe overall characteristics of the Sun such as composition, size, and main energy radiated. This is only tangentially related to the Sun's characteristics.

copy.en: The Sun is a star and the closest one to us! It looks bigger and brighter than other stars only because it is so much closer.
copy.tl: Ang Araw ay isang bituin (star) at pinakamalapit sa atin! Mukha itong mas malaki at maliwanag kaysa ibang bituin dahil lang mas malapit ito.
copy.bis: Ang Adlaw usa ka bituon (star) ug labing duol kanato! Morag mas dako ug masanag kini kaysa ubang bituon tungod lang kay mas duol kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it shoots out a glowing, sticky cloud to confuse predators
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not an example of mimicry or camouflage as animals changed to better suit their environment.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not living things interacting through competition or predation.

copy.en:
How does the vampire squid escape predators?

Instead of ink, it shoots out a glowing, sticky cloud to confuse predators!
copy.tl:
Paano tumatakas ang vampire squid sa mandaragit?

Sa halip na tinta, nagpapalabas ito ng nagliliwanag na malagkit na ulap para lituhin ang mandaragit!
copy.bis:
Giunsa paglayas sa vampire squid gikan sa manunukob?

Imbis tinta, mobuga kini og nagdan-ag nga pikit nga panganod aron libugon ang manunukob!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: eat different foods from all three food groups
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses eating a variety of foods from three food groups, which is a nutrition/health concept. It does not teach students to identify basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter). The card assumes food is a need but does not directly support the competency's skill of identifying basic needs.

copy.en: No single food has every nutrient your body needs, so eat different foods from all three food groups.
copy.tl: Walang iisang pagkain na may lahat ng sustansyang kailangan ng katawan, kaya kumain ng iba't ibang pagkain mula sa tatlong grupo.
copy.bis: Walay usa lang ka pagkaon nga adunay tanang sustansya nga gikinahanglan sa lawas, busa kaon og lain-laing pagkaon gikan sa tulo ka grupo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Vascular bundles are strands inside stems and leaves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different seasons in the Philippines and suggest activities that are appropriate for each season
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes plant vascular tissue (xylem and phloem) and has no connection to seasons in the Philippines or appropriate seasonal activities.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Vascular bundles are strands inside stems and leaves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about plant transport structures, not weather characteristics such as temperature, pressure, wind, humidity, rain, or cloud cover.

copy.en: Vascular bundles are strands inside stems and leaves that contain both xylem and phloem, acting as the plant's transport highway.
copy.tl: Ang vascular bundles ay mga hibla sa loob ng tangkay at dahon na naglalaman ng xylem at phloem, nagsisilbing transport highway ng halaman.
copy.bis: Ang vascular bundles mao ang mga hilo sa sulod sa punoan ug dahon nga adunay xylem ug phloem, nagsilbing transport highway sa tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the fuel energy is shared among many people
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses fuel energy being shared among passengers to improve per-person efficiency. It does not teach that energy can cause change, nor does it address light, sound, or heat energy as required by G4-F-9. The mention of 'energy' is only a broad connection.

copy.en:
Why is a jeepney carrying many passengers more fuel-efficient per person?

A jeepney is more fuel-efficient per passenger because the fuel energy is shared among many people, unlike single-occupancy travel!
copy.tl:
Bakit mas fuel-efficient ang jeepney na nagdadala ng maraming pasahero bawat tao?

Mas episyente ang jeepney bawat pasahero dahil ang enerhiya ng gasolina ay nahahati sa mas maraming tao, kumpara sa paglalakbay ng tig-iisa!
copy.bis:
Nganong mas fuel-efficient ang jeepney nga nagdala og daghang pasahero matag tawo?

Mas episyente ang jeepney matag pasahero tungod kay ang enerhiya sa gasolina gibahin sa mas daghang tawo, kaysa paglakbay nga nag-inusara!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That's thrust! For cars, it's wheels gripping the road; for ships, a propeller; and for jets, exhausted gases!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces act between objects and can be measured
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes thrust as a force that propels vehicles, giving examples of how it acts between objects (wheels/road, propeller/water, gases/jet). However, it does not address the measurement of forces, which is a key part of the competency. It only touches on the concept of a force acting between objects, but without any instructional support for measuring forces.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That's thrust! For cars, it's wheels gripping the road; for ships, a propeller; and for jets, exhausted gases!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces cause objects to accelerate, and that acceleration of an object is its rate of change of velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains thrust as a propulsive force but does not mention acceleration or the rate of change of velocity. It does not directly support the competency's focus on forces causing acceleration and defining acceleration. The content is only tangentially related to forces and motion.

copy.en:
What pushes a vehicle forward?

That's thrust! For cars, it's wheels gripping the road; for ships, a propeller; and for jets, exhausted gases!
copy.tl:
Ano ang tumutulak sa sasakyan pasulong?

Iyon ang thrust! Sa kotse, galing ito sa gulong; sa barko, sa propeller; at sa jet, sa exhausted gases!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang nagduso sa sasakyan pasulong?

Mao na ang thrust! Sa kotse, gikan sa gulong; sa barko, sa propeller; ug sa jet, sa exhausted gases!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the area beneath the line equals the total distance the object has traveled
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: construct and annotate distance-time graphs and velocity-time graphs to represent uniform and non-uniform acceleration
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a property of velocity-time graphs (area under the line equals distance), but the competency requires constructing and annotating distance-time and velocity-time graphs to represent uniform and non-uniform acceleration. The card does not address graph construction, annotation, or acceleration, and only shares a related interpretation fact.

copy.en: On a velocity-time graph, the area beneath the line equals the total distance the object has traveled!
copy.tl: Sa velocity-time graph, ang lawak sa ilalim ng linya ay katumbas ng kabuuang layong nilakbay ng bagay!
copy.bis: Sa velocity-time graph, ang lawak sa ilalom sa linya parehas sa kinatibuk-ang gilay-on nga gilaktan sa butang!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Animals use venom for two reasons: to hunt their food, or to defend themselves from enemies.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes current uses of venom (hunting and defense) but does not address how animals have changed over time to better suit their environment, which is the core of G5-L-9 (adaptation such as mimicry or camouflage). Venom as a trait is only tangentially related to adaptation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Animals use venom for two reasons: to hunt their food, or to defend themselves from enemies.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions hunting food, which relates to the basic need of food, but it does not identify or describe basic needs (air, food, water, shelter) as a concept. It only gives a reason for venom use, not instruction on basic needs of living things.

copy.en:
Why do some animals have venom?

Animals use venom for two reasons: to hunt their food, or to defend themselves from enemies.
copy.tl:
Bakit may kamandag ang ibang hayop?

Ginagamit ng mga hayop ang kamandag para mangaso ng pagkain, o para ipagtanggol ang sarili laban sa kaaway.
copy.bis:
Ngano adunay kamandag ang ubang hayop?

Ang mga hayop mogamit og kamandag aron mangayam og pagkaon, o aron manalipod sa ilang kaugalingon batok sa kaaway.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it has the highest density of shore-fish species per area
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the advantage of high biodiversity in maintaining the stability of an ecosystem during difficult conditions, such as food shortages, disease, and climate change
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that Verde Island Passage has the highest density of shore-fish species, i.e., high biodiversity. It does not explain the advantage of high biodiversity in maintaining ecosystem stability during difficult conditions such as food shortages, disease, or climate change. The content is about biodiversity but not the specific advantage required by the competency.

copy.en: Verde Island Passage, between Batangas and Mindoro, is recognized as the world's center of marine biodiversity — it has the highest density of shore-fish species per area!
copy.tl: Ang Verde Island Passage sa pagitan ng Batangas at Mindoro ay kilala bilang sentro ng marine biodiversity ng mundo — may pinakamaraming species ng dalampasigang isda sa bawat sukat na lugar!
copy.bis: Ang Verde Island Passage taliwala sa Batangas ug Mindoro giila isip sentro sa marine biodiversity sa kalibutan — adunay pinakataas nga density sa mga shore-fish species kada lugar!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Before a solution is used everywhere, scientists test it on a small scale first to see if it really works.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of the solute and solvent in a solution
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses testing a proposed solution/idea on a small scale; it does not address the role of solute and solvent in a chemical solution.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Before a solution is used everywhere, scientists test it on a small scale first to see if it really works.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe uniform or non-uniform mixtures, solutions, or suspensions; 'solution' here refers to a proposed fix, not a chemical mixture.

copy.en: Before a solution is used everywhere, scientists test it on a small scale first to see if it really works.
copy.tl: Bago gamitin ang isang solusyon kahit saan, sinusubok muna ito ng mga scientist sa maliit na sukat para makita kung talagang gumagana ito.
copy.bis: Sa dili pa gamiton ang usa ka solusyon bisan asa, sulayan una kini sa mga scientist sa gamay nga sukod aron makita kon tinuod ba kini nga molihok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the African nightcrawler worm is the one often used to make vermicompost
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify issues and concerns in the local community and how they could be addressed by science, such as the treatment of waste
assignedReviews.reason: Naming a vermicompost worm is not identifying a local waste-treatment issue addressed by science.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the African nightcrawler worm is the one often used to make vermicompost
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: Naming a compost worm species is not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the African nightcrawler worm is the one often used to make vermicompost
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate proper handling and disposal of materials according to their properties, such as reusing objects, disposing of excess oil into garbage, and recycling paper, plastic or glass
assignedReviews.reason: Naming a vermicompost worm is not demonstrating proper handling and disposal of materials.

copy.en: In the Philippines, the African nightcrawler worm is the one often used to make vermicompost.
copy.tl: Sa Pilipinas, ang bulateng African nightcrawler ang kadalasang ginagamit sa paggawa ng vermicompost.
copy.bis: Sa Pilipinas, ang African nightcrawler nga bulate ang kasagarang gigamit sa paghimo og vermicompost.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A vibration is a super fast back-and-forth movement!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines vibration as rapid back-and-forth movement but does not connect it to sound production or transfer, nor mention everyday sound situations like a ringing bell or hearing noises. It provides background knowledge needed to later understand that sound is caused by vibrations, but does not directly teach the competency.

copy.en: A vibration is a super fast back-and-forth movement! It’s when an object wiggles quickly around its resting spot.
copy.tl: Ang bibrasyon ay mabilis na pabalik-balik na paggalaw! Ito yung pag-wiggle ng isang bagay sa paligid ng pwesto nito.
copy.bis: Ang bibrasyon mao ang paspas nga pabalik-balik nga paglihok! Kini ang pag-wiggle sa butang palibot sa pahulay nga posisyon niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's a technique where you slightly oscillate your finger to rapidly vary the pitch
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a performance technique that changes pitch, but it does not explain how sound is made or transferred, nor does it address everyday sound situations like bells or noises.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: rapidly vary the pitch
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: research using secondary sources to identify how the properties of waves are described using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions pitch but does not use or explain scientific wave terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, or velocity, and it is not a research-based description of wave properties.

copy.en:
What is vibrato when playing string instruments?

It's a technique where you slightly oscillate your finger to rapidly vary the pitch, giving the sound an expressive, warm quality!
copy.tl:
Ano ang vibrato sa pagtugtog ng string instruments?

Ito ay teknik kung saan magpapalibo ka ng daliri para mabilis magbago ng pitch, na nagbibigay ng expressive at warm na quality sa tunog!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang vibrato sa pagtogtog sa string instruments?

Kini usa ka teknik dihin magpalibo ka sa tudlo aron paspas magbag-o sa pitch, nga nagahatag og expressive ug warm nga quality sa tunog!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify common acids, bases, and salts (e.g., hydrochloric acid, sodium hydroxide, and saline solution) using different indicators

copy.en:
What is the main chemical found in the vinegar in your kitchen?

The main chemical in vinegar is acetic acid, and its formula is CH3COOH!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pangunahing kemikal na makikita sa suka sa kusina mo?

Ang pangunahing kemikal sa suka ay acetic acid, at ang pormula nito ay CH3COOH!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pangunang kemikal nga makita sa suka sa imong kusina?

Ang pangunang kemikal sa suka kay acetic acid, ug ang pormula niini kay CH3COOH!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Vinegar is an acid called acetic acid
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify solutions, which can be found at home and in school and that react with litmus indicator, as acids, bases, and salts
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies vinegar as an acid found at home, which is a relevant example, but it does not mention litmus indicator or the reaction that identifies acids, bases, or salts. It only states a fact about vinegar, not the identification skill required by the competency.

copy.en:
What is the special acid found in vinegar?

Vinegar is an acid called acetic acid, and it is super useful in cooking our favorite meals!
copy.tl:
Anong espesyal na asido ang nasa suka?

Ang suka ay isang asido na tinatawag na acetic acid, at ito ay ginagamit sa pagluluto ng masasarap!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang espesyal nga asido nga naa sa suka?

Ang suka usa ka asido nga gitawag og acetic acid, ug kini gamiton sa pagluto sa lami nga pagkaon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Vinegar is an acid because it contains acetic acid
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify solutions, which can be found at home and in school and that react with litmus indicator, as acids, bases, and salts
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that vinegar is an acid, but the competency requires identifying solutions found at home/school that react with litmus indicator as acids, bases, or salts. No litmus indicator or reaction is mentioned, so the card does not directly support the skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Vinegar is an acid because it contains acetic acid
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify common acids, bases, and salts (e.g., hydrochloric acid, sodium hydroxide, and saline solution) using different indicators
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies vinegar as an acid, which is a common acid, but the competency requires identifying common acids, bases, and salts using different indicators. No indicator use or identification procedure is present, so the card only provides related factual content.

copy.en:
Why does vinegar taste so sour?

Vinegar is an acid because it contains acetic acid, which gives it that sour taste!
copy.tl:
Bakit napakaasim ng lasa ng suka?

Ang suka ay isang asido dahil naglalaman ito ng acetic acid, kaya maasim ang lasa nito!
copy.bis:
Nganong aslom kaayo ang suka?

Ang suka usa ka asido kay naa kini acetic acid, mao nga aslom ang lasa niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Vinegar is sour and acidic, which stops most spoilage bacteria from growing!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions food preservation via acidity but does not address factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions (e.g., concentration, temperature, surface area). It only states that acidity stops bacteria, which is not about reaction rates.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Vinegar is sour and acidic
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify common acids, bases, and salts (e.g., hydrochloric acid, sodium hydroxide, and saline solution) using different indicators
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies vinegar as acidic but does not identify it using indicators, nor does it name common acids, bases, or salts beyond vinegar. It does not teach the identification skill required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Vinegar is sour and acidic
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify solutions, which can be found at home and in school and that react with litmus indicator, as acids, bases, and salts
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions vinegar as an acidic solution found at home, but it does not discuss litmus indicator reactions or classification of acids, bases, and salts. It only states a property without the required identification method.

copy.en:
Why does vinegar help preserve food?

Vinegar is sour and acidic, which stops most spoilage bacteria from growing!
copy.tl:
Bakit nakakatulong ang suka sa pagpreserba ng pagkain?

Ang suka ay maasim at acidic, kaya pinipigilan nito ang pagdami ng maraming bakterya!
copy.bis:
Nganong makatabang ang suka sa pagpreserba sa pagkaon?

Ang suka aslom ug acidic, mao nga gipugngan niini ang pagdako sa kadaghanang bakterya!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a virus can't eat or grow on its own like other living things
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions growth as a characteristic but only to argue viruses lack it, and does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) as required. It is a debate about virus status, not instruction on living-thing characteristics.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Scientists still debate whether viruses are truly alive
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the difference between living and non-living things and give examples of each that can be found in the local environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on the living/non-living distinction but does not observe or describe the difference with local examples. It focuses on the scientific debate about viruses, which is not the grade 3 skill of comparing living and non-living things in the local environment.

copy.en:
Are viruses actually alive?

Scientists still debate whether viruses are truly alive, since a virus can't eat or grow on its own like other living things.
copy.tl:
Buhay ba talaga ang virus?

Pinagtatalunan ng mga siyentipiko kung buhay ba ang virus, dahil hindi ito kumakain o lumalaki nang mag-isa tulad ng ibang nilalang.
copy.bis:
Buhi ba jud ang bayrus?

Gilantugian sa mga siyentista kon buhi ba ang bayrus, kay dili kini mokaon o motubo nga mag-inusara sama sa ubang buhing binuhat.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it cannot grow, move, or multiply on its own
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions growth and multiplication as characteristics, but it does not teach the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) for typical organisms. It focuses on viruses being inactive outside a host, which is a specialized topic not aligned with Grade 3 content. The mention of 'grow' and 'multiply' is incidental and does not provide direct instructional support for describing the characteristics of living things.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Outside a living cell, a virus seems lifeless
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the difference between living and non-living things and give examples of each that can be found in the local environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on the living/non-living distinction by saying a virus seems lifeless outside a cell, but it does not describe the difference between living and non-living things in general or give examples from the local environment. The focus is on viruses, which is not a Grade 3 topic, and the card does not support the competency's requirement to observe and describe the difference with local examples.

copy.en:
Is a virus alive outside the body?

Outside a living cell, a virus seems lifeless — it cannot grow, move, or multiply on its own.
copy.tl:
Buhay ba ang virus sa labas ng katawan?

Sa labas ng buhay na selula, tila walang buhay ang virus — hindi ito tumutubo, lumilipat, o dumarami.
copy.bis:
Buhi ba ang virus sa gawas sa lawas?

Sa gawas sa buhing selula, daw walay kinabuhi ang virus — dili kini makatubo, makalihok, o makadaghan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: drink lots of water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card is home care advice for dengue and only incidentally mentions drinking water. It does not teach identifying the basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Paracetamol can ease the fever
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions fever, which is related to body temperature, but it does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems or explain indicators such as body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure. How does your skin make vitamin D?

Your skin has a natural substance that changes into vitamin D when hit by the sun's UV rays — like a tiny factory powered by sunlight!
copy.tl:
Paano nagagawa ng balat ang vitamin D?

May natural na sangkap sa balat mo na nagiging vitamin D kapag tinamaan ng UV na sinag ng araw — parang gamit itong pagawaan ng bitamina!
copy.bis:
Giunsa paghimo sa panit ang vitamin D?

Ang imong panit adunay natural nga sangkap nga mahimong vitamin D kon maigo sa UV nga sidlak sa adlaw — sama sa gamay nga pabrika sa bitamina!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: doctors may give vitamin D drops or tablets to make sure the body gets enough
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses vitamin D supplementation when sun or food is insufficient. It does not teach the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter) or help students identify those needs. The mention of food and sun is only as sources of vitamin D, not as basic needs, so it is only topically related.

copy.en: When sun or food isn't enough, like for tiny babies or people who stay indoors a lot, doctors may give vitamin D drops or tablets to make sure the body gets enough.
copy.tl: Kapag hindi sapat ang araw o pagkain — halimbawa sa maliliit na sanggol o taong palaging nasa loob — minsan nagbibigay ang doktor ng patak o tableta ng vitamin D para tiyaking sapat ang nakukuha ng katawan.
copy.bis: Kung dili igo ang adlaw o pagkaon — pananglitan sa gagmayng masuso o tawo nga kanunay sa sulod — usahay maghatag ang doktor og patak o tableta nga vitamin D aron masiguro nga igo ang nakuha sa lawas.

copy.en: Vitamin E helps protect the body's cells, and we get it from nuts and plant seeds.
copy.tl: Ang bitamina E ay tumutulong protektahan ang mga selula ng katawan, at makukuha ito sa mani at buto ng halaman.
copy.bis: Ang bitamina E motabang sa pagpanalipod sa mga selula sa lawas, ug makuha kini sa mani ug liso sa tanom.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions eating food but does not teach that food (along with air, water, shelter) is a basic need of living things. It focuses on vitamins coming from food, which is nutrition content, not the identification of basic needs.

copy.en: Most vitamins come from foods made by plants and animals, so we have to get them by eating.
copy.tl: Karamihan sa mga bitamina ay nagmumula sa pagkaing galing sa halaman at hayop, kaya kailangan nating kainin ang mga ito.
copy.bis: Kadaghanan sa mga bitamina naggikan sa pagkaon gikan sa mga tanom ug mananap, mao nga kinahanglan natong kan-on kini.

The card does not support that discussion/suggestion activity.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Which vitamin comes from sunlight?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe sources of light and their use in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about vitamin D production in the skin, not about describing sources of light or their everyday uses. Sunlight is mentioned only as a trigger for vitamin D, so it does not directly teach light sources or uses.

copy.en:
Which vitamin comes from sunlight?

Vitamin D is unusual — it doesn't only come from food. Your own skin makes it when sunlight hits you, so a little morning sun really helps.
copy.tl:
Aling bitamina galing sa araw?

Iba ang Vitamin D — hindi lang ito galing sa pagkain. Ginagawa mismo ng balat mo kapag naaraw ka, kaya mahalaga ang kaunting umagang araw.
copy.bis:
Unsang bitamina gikan sa adlaw?

Lahi ang Vitamin D — dili lang kini gikan sa pagkaon. Ang imong panit mismo maghimo niini kon mainitan ka, mao nga importante ang gamayng buntag nga adlaw.
